title: Fix the Read-Mode Write Attempt
description: The program should write a line of text to a new file.
expectedBehavior: The program should create log.txt (if needed) and write 'Log entry' into it.
actualProblem: The file is opened in "r" (read-only) mode, so fprintf() silently fails to write anything to it — no error is thrown, but the write simply has no effect, and if the file doesn't already exist, fopen itself returns NULL.
explanation: The mode string passed to fopen() determines what operations are allowed: "r" only permits reading (and requires the file to already exist), while "w" opens the file for writing, creating it if necessary. Writing requires the correct mode.
